FN-INHF6Z-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 175
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 04/11/2023
Senate Bill 175 as introduced would create the ReEngage Alabama Grant Program to: (1)
increase the number of Alabama adults with college degrees; (2) encourage adults meeting
certain requirements to return to college and complete degree programs connected with
workforce development needs and aligned with the state's high demand list; and (3) provide
financial assistance to adult learners in the state to complete their postsecondary education. This
will increase the obligations of: (1) the Alabama Commission on Higher Education (ACHE) to
implement and administer the provisions of this bill by a department estimated one-time start-up
cost of $1.5 million; and (2) ) the Education Trust Fund, contingent upon appropriation by the
Legislature, to provide grants to eligible adult learners in the amounts of $3,000 per semester
and $1,500 per semester for attendance at authorized four-year and two-year institutions,
respectively, to defray the cost of tuition and mandatory fees. According to the Commission,
$4.5 million would be needed annually to fund the grant program based on the number of
eligible students and high demand programs that have been identified.

FN-INHF6Z-4
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 175
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 05/24/2023
Senate Bill 175 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means Education would create the
Alabama Short-Term Credential Scholarship Program to provide grants of up to $4,500 to
eligible students to be applied toward the student's qualifying educational expenses to obtain
certain training at an Alabama Community College System (ACCS) institution. This bill would
increase the administrative obligations of: (1) ACCS to implement and administer the provisions
of this bill and to ensure that all funding provided be expended for the sole purpose of paying
the educational expenses; and (2) Alabama Department of Revenue to ensure that the
cumulative amount of grants issued not exceed $7 million annually.
Additionally, this bill would create the Short-Term Credential Scholarship Fund within the State
Treasury which would accept appropriations from the Legislature and fund the grants provided
by this program. This bill would provide that the program would be effective January 1, 2024
through December 31, 2028, unless extended by an act of the legislature.
